summary: An academic monograph on thögal ('Skullward Leap') that argues a historical thesis, but along the way translates and closely paraphrases the primary instructions. It describes the sky-gazing set-up; the six key points of gaze, posture, breath and awareness; lists of postures (lion, elephant, ascetic, goose, crystal antelope) and gazes (upward, straight, downward, right, left); the first appearances as circular 'seminal nuclei' and 'linked chains' likened to sheep, and how the yogi is told to stabilise them; instructions to press the eyeballs with the fingers to bring on the first lights; play with crystals as an introduction; and where the classical texts treat dark retreat. It also discusses the four visions in sequence. Much of the book is argument about origins and can be skipped.
why_relevant: Open-access conduit for primary thögal instructions on gaze, posture, eye pressure and the first lights, including what is done to induce them; the argument itself is out of scope.
